method: same topics/params as trial 1 (recon_probe semantic=True, start_year=2022, limit=10); content-addressed cache guarantees byte-identical pools, so all deltas are downstream harness changes. 6 parallel agents, one per domain.

clinical/oncology.topic: machine learning for early detection of pancreatic cancer

robotics.topic: vision-language models for household robot manipulation

climate.topic: attribution of extreme precipitation events to climate change

fintech.topic: causal inference for credit risk assessment in digital lending

education.topic: learning analytics dashboards for self-regulated learning

materials.topic: machine-learned interatomic potentials for lithium-ion battery materials

outcomes.P5_pool_floor: fired on exactly the two sub-floor pools (fintech n=8, materials n=6) -> 'thin'; 4/4 normal pools -> 'sufficient'. Zero false positives.
outcomes.P2_purity: 4/4 topic-bearing pools -> 'coherent' (0.53-0.80); 2/2 topic-less pools -> 'indeterminate' (never a false 'fragmented/0').
outcomes.P1_junk_filter: purged both known fragments: 'reduces default probability' (fintech) and '11 kcal mol' (materials).
outcomes.P1_family_diversity: family duplicates removed in 4/4 domains where they existed (oncology pdac, robotics plural LLM, climate extreme-weather-events, education singular dashboard); each replaced by a distinct, more informative term.
outcomes.P3: not exercised in this trial (lexicon path); covered by unit + E2E regression tests instead.
outcomes.residual: materials still yields fragmentary off-topic terms ('absolute solvation free', 'alchemical relative free') because the POOL is thin/off-topic (6 docs, 0 topics) -- now correctly flagged 'thin' so they cannot masquerade as trustworthy directions. This is a retrieval-quality limit, not a ranker defect.

verdict: All four changes behaved as specified on real cached pools. The two improvements are orthogonal and compose: P5/P2 decide whether a pool is trustworthy; P1 makes the top-3 diverse and clean when it is. The remaining failure mode (thin/off-topic retrieval) is now loudly surfaced rather than silently emitting junk.
